findings.title: Deleting cache leaves the connected-calendar query stale
findings.body: The delete mutation only shows a toast and invokes an optional callback; it does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Since `onSuccess` is optional, a successful deletion can leave the cached response showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and delete action until the page is reloaded. Invalidate the query on success so the UI reflects the deleted cache.

findings.title: Legacy cache timestamps are set to the migration time
findings.body: Adding this column with `DEFAULT NOW()` assigns the migration timestamp to every existing cache row, not the time that row was actually last updated. The cache-status query uses this field and the UI labels it “Last updated,” so existing credentials will appear to have refreshed at deployment even when their data is old or expired. Backfill a meaningful timestamp or avoid presenting the synthetic value as the actual update time.

findings.title: The environment-file path depends on the caller's working directory
findings.body: `ENV_FILE` is resolved relative to the current directory, not the script's location. Invoking this script from the repository root (for example, `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) targets `../.env` outside the checkout instead of the repository's `.env`, so the application will not use the configured webhook URL. Resolve the path relative to the script or explicitly change directories.

findings.title: The environment update uses BSD-only sed syntax
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is the BSD/macOS form of in-place editing. On GNU/Linux, the empty argument is treated as a script or input path and the command fails, leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` unchanged. Use a portable in-place update or handle the platform-specific syntax.
